lines.text: The emergency number 112.
In case of danger to life [levensgevaar] you call 112, day and night.
For example: an accident [ongeluk] has happened and someone is no longer responding.
You say where an ambulance is needed; it arrives within fifteen minutes.
The operator tells you what to do until the ambulance arrives.
You also call 112 for the police or the fire brigade [brandweer].
Needing your huisarts urgently.
You call your own huisarts or dentist on working days between 8:00 and 17:00 — those are the office hours [kantoortijden].
Is help needed quickly but there is no danger to life (for example: your child has fallen down the stairs)?
You get a phone menu [keuzemenu] and can key in [intoetsen] a number for urgency/emergency [spoed].
The assistant can also call an ambulance.
Outside office hours.
Do you need a doctor outside office hours, for example if your child has a high fever [koorts] at the weekend?
Then you call the out-of-hours GP service [huisartsenpost, also called huisartsen-spoedpost].
Doctors work there, usually in the hospital.
You find the number on your huisarts's website or on Google with your place of residence [woonplaats].
If you call your own huisarts outside office hours, you get an answering machine [antwoordapparaat] with information and a phone number.
For the dentist there is also an emergency number.
Emergency department [Spoedeisende Hulp, SEH].
The huisarts or huisartsenpost sometimes sends you urgently to the hospital, to the emergency department [afdeling Spoedeisende Hulp].
In an emergency situation [noodsituatie] you can also go to the SEH without an appointment.
People who need help quickly are seen first; otherwise you may wait longer.
In summary: danger to life → 112; urgent help during office hours → huisarts, number for spoed; urgent help outside office hours → huisartsenpost; emergency situation → go to the SEH yourself.
